items.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview
items.q: Big Bill Broonzy. It was all blues dates.

ctx.x: But that's when I got my first, real bass violin. I was still going to school, high school, junior high, and Buster got a record date for me. I'll never forget this. And I had to get permission from my teacher to make it, although I'm working every night. We worked from, say, about 9 or 10 o' clock at night until the owner said, Mr. Robinson said, "You could go home now." That means if there were 2 people left in the club, we have to play until they got ready to leave, and it might be daylight. I think I was…

And he was taking half of that for my fiddle. But I enjoyed it; I was getting a world of experience. And Buster had this record date for this guy named Melrose Mellow's, and I didn't realize who the fellow was -- Big Bill -- we made a

record called "WPA" and in later years I found out it was out of print. But I remember I played all that afternoon -- it was all blues, nothing but blues. Big Bill Broonzy. It was all blues dates. I don't know who the other blues guy -- they kept me on it, you know, I was what you might say the house bassist. I think I made $10, which was good money. I made only $10 a week.
